en: You learned <Color:9>Meteor Strike (Climax Heat)<Color:Default>.
Big moves can also be your greatest defense if it means you can take out an enemy before he strikes.
I learned how to step forward with my left leg while my right leg was still off the ground.
That would mean you were floating in midair like a ninja. Wait, is that a ninja thing or not?
With all those grenades you made me dodge, I felt so light on my feet. The lightest ever.
You learned <Color:9>Launch Strike Plus<Color:Default>.
If you don't give your enemy an opportunity to counterattack, it's more effective than hardening your defenses.
Yeah, yeah, I'll keep that in mind. But I was wondering...
What, you have a question? If you have a question, raise your hand.
Yeah. Aren't you going to go see your wife and daughter now that you're back in Japan?
You said before that you can't go home, but why not?
You can't stop fixating on matters that have nothing to do with your mission, can you?
It's just, you used to talk about your daughter like she was everything to you.
Talking about one's family is almost a taboo on the battlefield, but...
I... didn't return to the Middle East just to polish my skills.
Wow, you're being unusually serious.
Mercenaries like me end up learning things⑬things that many would rather keep hidden.
And being mercenaries, once a war is over, we're about as useful as a car without wheels.
In short, we're expendable, but we also have top-secret information that stays with us as we return to our home countries.
I could see how that could be a problem.
As a mercenary field commander, I was no exception.
I was privy to top-secret info relating to the nation that hired me, and they didn't consider confidentiality until the war was over.
But then my former employer started to worry about damaging secrets getting out.
Are you saying...
Exactly. I didn't feel safe here and decided to leave the country for a while.
I see. You left because you don't want to get your family involved.
I can't go into the details, as that would put you at risk, too.
And needless to say, let's keep this between you and me. Understood?
Relax, we moneylenders are quite discreet. It's part of doing business.
I'll take your word on that. Now, enough of this idle chat.
Dismissed!
Dismissed⑬ No, wait.
What? Something wrong?
I think we're being watched.
Man, you're just being paranoid. We were just talking about clandestine spy stuff, after all.
No, I feel an ominous stare on me. I have felt this many times... right before a sniper opens fire.
A sniper!? What've you dragged me into!?
Quiet! Listen to me carefully. When I give the signal, spring back and hide in the shadows.
Three... two... one... now!
Whoa, you weren't kidding. What the hell's going on here?
We should be okay for now. Once a sniper loses the element of surprise, he usually backs off until the next time.
I'll have to take your word on that.
It didn't take them long to discover that I was back in Japan.
You mean the people you were talking about? The ones who want to keep you quiet?
That's the most likely scenario, and the worst possible one, too.
If they figure out I know they're after me, they might go after my family to draw me out.
Are we talking about a hostage situation here!? This is bad.
I can't warn my family, either, because that could reveal their location.
I'll have to put an end to this myself.
I'm sorry, Akiyama-kun. I didn't mean to drag you into all this.
Truth be told, I never expected anything involving you to take such a serious turn.
But this is no laughing matter. If there's anything I can do to help, let me know.
I appreciate that. You be careful now, okay?
As for me, I'll avoid making any big moves for now. Better to assess the situation first.
Well, dismissed.
I stole the enemy's new mobile weaponized suit and won a battle up in the stratosphere.
Sounds like a sci-fi movie! But if you have access to those sorts of weapons, why even bother with training?
When you're surrounded, and the enemy's unloading on you, your only chance is to quickly exploit a gap in your enemy's defenses.
You learned <Color:9>Counter Kick<Color:Default>.
Even the most skilled enemies are vulnerable just as they begin an attack. Never fail to take advantage of that.
In short, we're expendable. But we also have top-secret information that stays with us as we return to our home countries.
I returned home despondent after my war buddy died in action, only to learn it was a prank.
That's a terrible prank. I mean, you were soldiers, not frat boys!
Even when things get chaotic, I need to keep looking for a chance to land a big blow.
You learned <Color:9>Final Drive (Climax Heat)<Color:Default>.
You don't get many chances to quickly finish off your enemy. Whether or not you can spot those chances will decide the tide of battle.
Roger that. By the way, what happened after that sniper incident?
I haven't learned anything more since then, and they don't seem to be watching me anymore.
Who are you!?
I must commend you, Daijiro Saigo. Few have ever been in my sights and lived to tell of it.
You're the sniper who shot at him!?
Shun Akiyama, owner of Sky Finance, I presume?
You've obviously done your homework.
I don't know how much Saigo has told you, but everyone who knows what he knows must be eliminated.
Whoa, whoa! Let's take this down a notch. I'm guessing that's not a toy gun... right?
Enough! Akiyama-kun doesn't know a thing!
It doesn't matter. Now that he knows about me, I can't let him live.
Just calm down and lower your weapon, okay? We can talk it over like civilized people.
Besides, how could I possibly benefit from telling anyone about you?
You're just wasting your breath. Once we have a target, we never fail to take them out. Not a single one has ever escaped.
Enough talk. I'm putting you both in the ground.
Saigo-san! Why'd you do that!?
Run, Akiyama-kun. You must live.
This can't be happening. It's all a bad dream, right?
Tell my family... Tell them I put up a good fight till the bitter end.
Saigo-san! Come on, Saigo-san!
Come on, this isn't funny...
You were supposed to go first, but no matter. You won't escape.
You'll meet Saigo again in hell.
You won't get away with this.
I'm not about to give up so easily, not after Saigo-san gave his life for me.
Well now, do you think you have a chance against me?
He may have had a military fetish and was always saying and doing strange things, but...
Saigo-san was a good man. He was working hard to teach young people about risk management.
And most of all, he treasured his family.
Why should I care about any of that?
I could say the same thing. What does any of this have to do with me?
I'm not letting you kill me! You're going to pay for what you did to Saigo-san!
And cut!
Oh, yeah! I'm going to cut loose on this bastard! Wait...
Cut? What do you mean, cut?
That was a great scene. You get all that?
That was an award-winning performance, Master! It almost moved me to tears!
Well all right, then! That's a wrap! We'll celebrate with some drinks tonight!
Um, excuse me. Would someone explain what's going on here?
You gave an amazing performance, too, Akiyama-kun! I'm talking Best Supporting Actor nomination!
I... What? I still don't get it.
Whatever. Listen up, Saigo-san. Listen carefully.
I have absolutely no idea what's going on here. None. Whatsoever.
I just saw you get shot to death... But now you're standing in front of me, perfectly fine.
Of course I am. That was a replica gun.
And the sniper?
One of my students.
And the guy who shouted, "Cut"?
Another one of my students. A member of my film crew to be exact.
What... What film crew?
Great question! They're helping me create promotional videos for my organization.
It's part of a series I'm calling "Daijiro Saigo's Life on the Battlefield"!
Are you telling me this was all fake? Part of some awful action movie!?
Fake? Awful!? Do you have a problem with the script I wrote, Akiyama-kun!?
I went through a lot of trouble to do this. I mean, I even got this hairpiece.
What!? That's why you're wearing a hairpiece?
Wait, so how long were you filming? I'm not sure what was real anymore.
The video starts with my student rushing to help me as I collapse, my last ounce of energy spent on the battlefield.
All the way back that far? You only collapsed because you were hungry!
With a few edits, that scene will really shine!
How is the editing coming along on the climax scene we just shot?
We have a rough cut ready. Akiyama-san's line is killer, too. Here.
"Saigo was a good man. He was working hard to teach young people about risk management."
Wait a second! You cut the part where I called him a strange guy with a military fetish!
That was epic, Akiyama-kun! You delivered that line like you were on some big budget TV show!
Oh, whatever. I'm too tired to argue.
Hey, don't be like that. I'll send you a copy once we're done.
Gee, thanks...
But I must say, I was really moved by how angry you got when you saw me die.
It's going to be tough living up to all that stuff you said.
Tough for you? You know how embarrassed I feel right now?
Listen, this video is just a way to promote my work. My core mission is teaching young people about the importance of risk management.
That's what I'm devoting my life to. I hope I'll live up to your expectations in that department.
I'm impressed, Saigo-san.
But you're not off the hook, either! You, too, must devote yourself to training hard every day!
And I'll be waiting here anytime you need to brush up.
Haha, I should've figured my training doesn't end here.
Still, you give good advice, Saigo-san. I'll take it to heart.
Did you get that!?
"You give good advice, Saigo-san."
Oh, I give up.
All right, Suicidal Shooting it is.
In this exercise, my students and I will shoot at you as you make your way from here to the goal.
You pass if you're able to take us out by returning fire.
So we'll be using guns?
What else would we use? I've got everything we need right here, don't worry.
I'm tired of stating the obvious, but don't you see any problem with waging a gun battle in the middle of town?
This is urban warfare training, so I'd say we're in the perfect place.
Of course, we'll be using replica guns. As much as I'd like to use live rounds, I felt we should do the neighbors a favor.
I actually agree with you for once.
All right then, begin!
Hold on! I just remembered something I have to do.
The battlefield waits for no one! Get your errands and bathroom breaks done beforehand!
But I'll make an exception this time. Come on back when you're ready.
Just the man I wanted to see! Ready for some training?
Not now. Maybe I'll come back later.
Oh, well all right, then. You know where to find me.
Yes, please.
<Color:7>Heat Actions are not available<Color:Default> in training battles. Make sure you are fully prepared, as Saigo's training can be demanding.
Okay, pick your poison.
Okay, let's move this elsewhere.
All right, Suicidal Running it is.
In this exercise, you'll chase me through the streets of Sotenbori. Catch me, and the training is complete.
But won't dashing around town like that be a major nuisance to others?
I have it covered. My students will be directing pedestrians and traffic to minimize potential problems.
That's an even bigger nuisance! Couldn't you have picked a more appropriate location?
Crap, you already have everyone in place. Fine, let's finish this before the cops come.
Relax. I've used this method of training before without causing any problems.
I think everyone's just too shocked to complain.
Okay. Let's get started!
Okay, let's get ready.
All right, Suicidal Combat it is.
In this exercise, we'll battle each other one-on-one, as if it were a real war.
This is an all-out, no-holds-barred battle. Defeat me, and you pass.
We stand here and hit each other? Sounds simple enough.
But it wouldn't be much of a training exercise if we slugged it out barehanded. That's why I'll be using a machine gun.
A machine gun!? You weren't kidding when you said this was called Suicidal Combat!
This is a high-performance replica gun that's been customized for training purposes. It'll definitely hurt, but it's not going to kill you.
If you're going to customize a special gun, why not make it so it doesn't hurt?
